tagline: The largest urban water market in America.
summary: New York Harbor is the biggest urban water-mobility opportunity in North America — Manhattan ringed by water with tens of millions of ferry trips a year, congestion pricing pushing trips off the road, and no fast premium airport-water link today.

use_cases.title: Cross-harbour commuting
use_cases.body: High-frequency Hudson (~2 nm) and East River (~1.5 nm) crossings, faster and cleaner than diesel ferry, PATH or road.

use_cases.title: Airport-water link
use_cases.body: A premium Midtown↔LaGuardia (~9 nm) foiling run over the East River — the link the city has never had.

use_cases.title: Hamptons summer run
use_cases.body: A long premium seasonal corridor to the East End (~95 nm).

journeys.with_navier: A premium foiling airport link over the river

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The harbour's commuter crossings (Hudson ~2 nm, East River ~1.5 nm, Midtown↔LaGuardia ~9 nm) are short and dense — inside the all-electric envelope and the high-frequency urban runs foiling transforms.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Carries the premium long-haul summer corridors (Manhattan↔Hamptons/Montauk ~95 nm) with no charging at the East End.

competitive_landscape: Today: Staten Island Ferry, NYC Ferry and private operators on diesel hulls. The pain is slow crossings, no airport link and a diesel fleet under decarbonization pressure — the status quo a faster, cleaner tier improves on.
seasonality: Year-round harbour operation; winter handled by sheltered routing, with the hybrid reserved for longer exposed summer corridors.
regulatory_note: NYC has aggressive transport-decarbonization targets and live Manhattan congestion pricing, both favouring zero-emission water. NYC Ferry is city-subsidised and procurement-driven — a clear public-transport pathway.

precedents.what: A foiling-electric vessel network at national scale (~100 vessels / $100M, 3-year phasing)
precedents.why_it_matters: Proves foiling-electric works as an at-scale transfer-and-island-hopping network, not just a pilot.
